## ✨ Highlights

- 🖥️ **`janusctl tui`: the node live, in the terminal** - CPU, memory and interfaces with their graphs, HAProxy's frontends, backends and servers, processes, services, modules, the node's events and a log, refreshed every two seconds; with a context of several nodes it opens on the fleet. The operator actions of the Controller's node page are there too - a server set ready, drain or maint, a reload, a reboot, a restart of janusd, a trial confirmed -, each asked first, offered by what your certificate may do. See [janusctl](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/janusctl.md#the-dashboard-janusctl-tui).
- ⚡ **A node boots faster, and can reboot without the firmware**: kernel and root filesystem compressed with zstd (the API listening a third sooner after the kernel started under KVM), `-kexec` on `system reboot` and `lifecycle upgrade` skips the POST, and the boot is measured (`janus_boot_stage_seconds`).
- 🔒 **Security release**: Go 1.26.9 and `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 fix a series of HTTP/2 and HTTP/1 server flaws - a crash, memory and CPU exhaustion, connections served on after a CONNECT - in what every Janus binary serves: janusd's API, the Controller, the exporter, the site. **Update the nodes, the Controller and janusctl.**

## 🖥️ The dashboard in the terminal

- **`janusctl tui`** shows one node the way bpytop shows a machine: CPU with its load, memory with what's used, cached and available, each interface's rates, HAProxy's process (version, uptime, connections, sessions per second, idle) over its frontends and its backends with their servers - status, weight, connections, rate, bytes, last check -, the processes with their CPU and memory, the services and their health, the modules present (VRRP's role and addresses, BGP's sessions, Consul, the firewall), a trial that would revert and when, and at the bottom the node's events or a log - janusd's or HAProxy's, both side by side on a terminal 120 columns wide. The digits show or hide a panel and the layout recomposes, `Tab` moves the focus, `↑↓` move in it, `s` and `r` sort, `+` and `-` set the interval (1 s to 30 s), `p` pauses, `?` lists the keys, `q` leaves.
- **The fleet**: a context of several nodes opens on one line per node - state, version, HAProxy, connections, sessions per second, CPU, memory, load, VRRP role, trials pending; `Enter` opens a node, `Esc` comes back; `-n NODE` goes straight to one. The nodes are asked in parallel, an unreachable one says why.
- **Actions**, each confirmed in a dialog: `Enter` on a server sets it ready, drain or maint; `R` reloads HAProxy; `B` reboots the node - through the firmware, a power cycle, or kexec; `J` restarts janusd; `C` confirms a network, firewall or sysctl trial that would otherwise revert. The footer offers only what the certificate's role may do: a reader sees everything but the logs, an operator acts, an admin confirms trials. What the node refuses is said as the node says it.
- **`janusctl tui -once`** prints one frame as plain text and exits - for a script, a ticket or a quick look over SSH. It asks the node twice a second apart, so the rates are real.
- **Where**: any terminal of 80×24 or more; colours follow `COLORTERM` and `TERM` (24-bit, 256 or 16 colours), `NO_COLOR` turns them off; `Ctrl-C`, a hang-up or a resize leave the terminal as they found it. Against a node of a previous release everything works but the processes' CPU, shown as `-` (the API field is new, below).

## ⚡ Faster boot

- **Boot time is measured**: init prints when the kernel handed over and when it started janusd; janusd logs `boot: api listening Ns after the kernel started (kernel, init, haproxy)` and the exporter serves `janus_boot_stage_seconds{stage}` ([metrics](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/metrics.md)). The firmware's own time comes before that clock. See [Boot time](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/architecture.md#boot-time).
- **Reboots and updates can skip the firmware**: `janusctl system reboot -kexec` and `janusctl lifecycle upgrade -kexec` (`RebootMode KEXEC` in the API) jump from the running kernel into the next one - seconds, where a server's POST takes a minute. Opt-in, see [updates](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/updates.md#with-janusctl): with Secure Boot on, only a signed release; a revert always goes through the firmware. Proven on Proxmox VE 9.2 (the API answers 3.4 s after the call, 7.3 s through the firmware). Known not to work on a libvirt machine with Secure Boot enabled under OVMF 2025.02 (Debian 13's package): the node comes back through the firmware after a crash of the kexec'd kernel; edk2 2026.08 is fine. Bare metal is untried.
- **The kernel and the root filesystem are compressed with zstd** instead of gzip and xz, and the root filesystem decompresses on every CPU. Under KVM the API listens a third sooner after the kernel started (1.5 s instead of 2.3 s on one host, 1.4 s instead of 2.0 s on another; HAProxy serving at 1.1 s instead of 1.9 s); the image is 7 % bigger. Nothing changes for an upgrade: a node takes the new kernel and root filesystem together.

## 🔒 Security

Every Janus binary - janusd, janusctl, the Controller and its updater, the site, the exporter and the node_exporter extension's own binary - is built with **Go 1.26.9** and **`golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0** (from 1.26.8 and v0.59.0). They fix, in what these binaries serve or call:

- **HTTP/2 servers** - janusd's gRPC API on `:9505`, the Controller's HTTPS and node pages: a crash on an HPACK encoder race (CVE-2026-97032), memory exhaustion through trailer headers (CVE-2026-78659, high), a double flow-control refund (CVE-2026-78663, critical), CPU exhaustion from repeated initial window changes (CVE-2026-78669, high), malformed framing headers accepted by the transport (CVE-2026-78660, high).
- **HTTP/1 servers and clients** - the exporter on `:10056`, the site, the Controller's registration port, the updater, janusd's own fetches: a connection served on after a 2xx answer to CONNECT (CVE-2026-94439, high) or after a rejected CONNECT (CVE-2026-56866, high), unbounded `Range` headers (CVE-2026-78667, high), a memory limit bypassed by MIME headers (CVE-2026-94440, high).
- **TLS and templates**: malformed ECH outer extension references rejected (CVE-2026-97031, high), two `html/template` escaping fixes (CVE-2026-94448, CVE-2026-97030); `os.Root` following junctions on Windows (CVE-2026-56857, critical) concerns no Janus binary, none runs there.

Of these, `govulncheck` finds the HPACK race and the CONNECT desynchronization on code paths janusd, the Controller, the exporter and the site actually run; the rest is fixed in code they don't appear to reach. **What to do**: update every node - the usual A/B update, whatever its HAProxy branch or kernel track: the fix is in janusd -, the Controller from its page, janusctl from apt or the release's `.deb`, and the Terraform provider from the release's archives.

## 🔧 Fixes

- A node that synchronized its clock in the first second of a boot reported itself unsynchronized a moment later, until the next NTP poll a minute or more on: the kernel drops the synchronized status when its clocksource changes (the TSC's refined calibration, right after boot), and nothing noticed. janusd now checks every 5 s between polls and synchronizes again at once - `janus_time_synchronized` and the RTC follow.
- A confirmation asked from inside a dialog of the Controller or of a node page - removing an SSH key from the account dialog, a second factor, a trusted browser - came up behind that dialog, which had to be closed to answer. It comes above it now.

## 🔌 The node API

- `SystemService.Reboot` takes a `reboot_mode`: `REBOOT_MODE_KEXEC` loads the active slot's kernel and reboots into it without the firmware; the node refuses, nothing rebooted, when it can't load it. `LifecycleService.Upgrade` takes the same `reboot_mode` for its final reboot, and falls back to the firmware - saying so in its `rebooting` stage - when kexec isn't possible.
- `SystemService.Processes`: each `ProcessInfo` carries `cpu_seconds`, the process's cumulative CPU time like `ProcessStat.cpu_seconds` - the rate is the difference between two samples. 0 from a node older than this release.
- Nothing removed or changed otherwise. [API reference](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/api-reference.md).

## 📦 Upstreams

- **BIRD 2.19.3** in the BGP extension (from 2.19.2).
- **Go 1.26.9** and **`golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0**, above - with `golang.org/x/sys` v0.48.0 and `golang.org/x/text` v0.42.0, which it depends on.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes**: the usual A/B update, from the Controller or `janusctl lifecycle upgrade` - with `-kexec` if you want to skip the firmware (opt-in; read the known limitation above). Nothing to change in a configuration.
- **Controller**: from v2026.10.07-3, the update is done from the page as usual - its updater gives the data to user 65532 and reports the start. **A Controller still before v2026.10.07-3 must first follow that release's by-hand upgrade notes**: updated from the page, it is put back by its updater (nothing lost).
- **janusctl**: `apt update && apt install janusctl`, or the release's `.deb` - for `janusctl tui` and the fixed TLS and HTTP code. The dashboard works against nodes of previous releases, but for the processes' CPU column.
- **Terraform provider**: rebuilt with Go 1.26.9, the release's archives.
